claims.claim: A University of Ottawa study tested the CCC+TL cosmology model and found it consistent with Big Bang nucleosynthesis observations.
claims.episode_span: A University of Ottawa study tested the CCC+TL cosmology model against several major cosmological observations. The research, published in the journal Universe, examined Big Bang nucleosynthesis consistency and found the model held up.
claims.source_title: Theory predicting an older universe without dark matter or dark energy passes key cosmological tests
claims.supporting_quote: An alternative model in which the universe is 26.7 billion years old and needs neither dark matter nor dark energy has held up against several major cosmology tests, according to a new University of Ottawa study.

claims.claim: NASA selected eight companies for the CLPS 2 framework with a combined maximum value of $10 billion over ten years.
claims.episode_span: Eight companies including Blue Origin, Firefly Aerospace, Intuitive Machines, ispace-U.S., Lockheed Martin Space, Northrop Grumman Space Systems, SpaceX and Voyager Technologies are eligible to compete for future lunar surface deliveries under the new CLPS 2 framework. The contract has a combined maximum value of $10 billion over ten years.
claims.source_title: NASA Awards Moon Base Transportation, Technology, Science Projects
claims.supporting_quote: The CLPS 2 framework is a 10-year, multiple-award, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity master contract with a combined maximum value of $10 billion.

claims.claim: Blue Origin received a $94 million base contract with a possible additional $140 million to deliver the PROMISE rover.
claims.episode_span: Blue Origin received a $94 million base contract, with a possible additional $140 million, to deliver the rover to the lunar south pole using its Mark 1 lander.
claims.source_title: NASA Awards Moon Base Transportation, Technology, Science Projects
claims.supporting_quote: NASA awarded Blue Origin a $94 million base contract, with an option period worth an additional $140 million based on performance to deliver PROMISE to the lunar South Pole.
